theArgumentAGAINSTADerivation_andHowItIs.objection: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 7.3's 2026-08-05 rider: a derivation TRANSCRIBES nothing but INHERITS everything, and inherited MEASUREMENTS go stale under the successor's name. That rider describes EXACTLY the defect this artifact repairs, so choosing a derivation to repair it is choosing the mechanism that produced it.
theArgumentAGAINSTADerivation_andHowItIs.answer: The rider does not forbid derivation. It states a requirement: 'a derivation must state, for every inherited measurement, either that it re-measured it or that it did not.' This artifact discharges that requirement explicitly at $.staleMeasurementSweep and $.inheritedMeasurementDisposition. A standalone would inherit the same measurements by RE-TYPING them, which is strictly worse: the figures would arrive with no predecessor to compare against and would be graded as the author's own.

resolutionAlgorithm.step1: Parse retention-tiers.v26.json with json.load under an object_pairs_hook that raises on any repeated key at any depth (IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 7.5).
resolutionAlgorithm.step2: Hard-compare the parsed value's canonical digest against predecessorCanonicalValueSha256, and the file's byte digest against predecessorSha256. Either mismatch is a REFUSAL, not a warning.
resolutionAlgorithm.step3: Apply each operation in order. Each 'set' names an EXISTING path whose current value must equal the operation's 'from' at EXACT JSON TYPE -- bool tested BEFORE int, because bool subclasses int in Python and hash(1.0) == hash(1) makes a bare == unsafe on either axis. A 'from' mismatch REFUSES the whole resolution; it never silently overwrites.
resolutionAlgorithm.step4: 'from' and 'to' must share a JSON type. No operation here changes a leaf's type.
resolutionAlgorithm.step5: The result is the resolved document. Its canonical digest must equal resolvedValue.sha256 below.
resolutionAlgorithm.whyRefuseRatherThanOverwrite: This is the check-c2-v9.py discipline. An operation that does not find what it claims to replace is describing a document that no longer exists, and applying it anyway would publish a resolution nobody verified.

resolvedValue.whatThisDigestIsOver: the CANONICAL SERIALISATION OF A PARSED VALUE. It is NOT a claim about any file's bytes and no file with these bytes need ever exist. Two encoders that disagree on key order, indentation or escaping still produce this digest, which is the point: a derivation's product is a VALUE.
resolvedValue.canonicalSerialisation: json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8'), then hashlib.sha256(...).hexdigest()

encodingNotesForAReimplementer.keyOrder: lexicographic by Unicode code point over the raw key strings
encodingNotesForAReimplementer.separators: ',' between members and ':' between key and value, with no spaces
encodingNotesForAReimplementer.nonAscii: emitted as raw UTF-8, never as \uXXXX escapes
encodingNotesForAReimplementer.nanAndInfinity: rejected, not emitted; the value contains neither
encodingNotesForAReimplementer.theSingleFloat: the resolved value contains exactly ONE float, at $.partC_retentionBounds.vectors.rows[6].bounds.keepCount. It appears under the recipe above as the 17-character canonical substring ["keepCount":200.0], whose value token is the five characters 200.0. A reimplementer whose float formatter emits 200 or 2.0e2 will get a different digest and MUST NOT conclude the resolution differs. Floats are formatted by Python's repr().
encodingNotesForAReimplementer.integersAndBooleans: JSON int and JSON true/false are distinct types here and are never interchanged

This block is therefore stated as a partition and verified in BOTH directions mechanically, and its verification result is published.
keyLocator.rule: Every top-level key of THIS DELTA FILE falls in exactly one of three classes: OPERATION-TARGET (named by an operation, so the resolved document carries it at the value stated here), RESTATED-IDENTICAL (present in the resolved document at a value this file repeats verbatim, hard-compared) or DELTA-ONLY (absent from the resolved document entirely). Every top-level key of the RESOLVED DOCUMENT that is in none of those classes is RESOLVED-ONLY -- present there and ABSENT here.

instrumentPosition.answer: NO. It cannot, and no amount of running it differently changes that.
instrumentPosition.why: It binds retention-tiers.v26.json BY NAME. Its GATED_PINS table hard-pins that filename at a6546408fb38df95166f0ec41b1d9d9dae0dbda580684ff8a6e94f57145ad97e with an exit-2-on-mismatch gate, its findings are emitted as 'N finding(s) in retention-tiers.v26.json', and its census constants (14 GATED, 5 ADVANCING, 1 DESTROYED, 2935 scalar leaves, 37 verbatim fields, 20 vectors, 24 invariants) are hand-transcribed literals about that document.
